questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Smooth plane sliding under gravity

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Direct application of Newton's second law on a smooth inclined plane

hints: Resolve weight parallel to the slope: the driving force down the plane is $mg\sin\theta$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve parallel to the smooth plane to find acceleration:
$$mg\sin 30^\circ = ma \implies a = g\sin 30^\circ = 10(0.5) = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Resolve perpendicular to the plane to find normal reaction $R$:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 4(10)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.6\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
On any smooth slope with no extra forces along the plane, the mass always cancels:
$$a = g\sin\theta = 10\sin 30^\circ = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

The normal reaction balances the perpendicular component of weight:
$$R = mg\cos\theta = 4 \times 10 \times \cos 30^\circ = 34.6\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves weight parallel to the plane to find acceleration: $mg\sin 30^\circ = ma \implies a = 10\sin 30^\circ = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Resolves perpendicular to the plane: $R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 4(10)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \approx 34.6\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 2: Applied force up a smooth slope

hints: Take up the plane as positive: the equation of motion is $P - mg\sin\theta = ma$.

walkthrough.text:

$$P - mg\sin 20^\circ = ma$$
$$P - 5(10)\sin 20^\circ = 5(1.5)$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
To accelerate up the slope, the pulling force must overcome the downhill component of weight and provide the acceleration:
$$P = mg\sin 20^\circ + ma$$

Substitute the given values:
$$P = 50(0.3420) + 5(1.5) = 17.10 + 7.5 = 24.6\text{ N}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Finding slope angle from distance and time

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 3: Inverting kinematics to find incline angle

hints: First use $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ to find acceleration $a$ down the plane.
Then relate acceleration to the angle using $a = g\sin\theta$.

walkthrough.text:
Use kinematics down the slope from rest:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 \implies 18.0 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}a(3.0^2) \implies 18.0 = 4.5a \implies a = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Link acceleration to the slope angle:
$$a = g\sin\theta \implies 4.0 = 10\sin\theta \implies \sin\theta = 0.40 \implies \theta = \sin^{-1}(0.40) \approx 23.6^\circ$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Start with kinematics along the line of greatest slope:
$$a = \frac{2s}{t^2} = \frac{2(18.0)}{9.0} = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

On a smooth plane without other forces, gravity provides all acceleration:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{a}{g} = \frac{4.0}{10} = 0.40 \implies \theta = 23.6^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses kinematics to find acceleration: $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 \implies 18.0 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}a(3^2) \implies a = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Equates $a = g\sin\theta \implies 4.0 = 10\sin\theta \implies \sin\theta = 0.40 \implies \theta = 23.6^\circ$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 6: Projection up an incline to instantaneous rest

hints: When projected up the slope, gravity causes deceleration: $a = -g\sin 30^\circ = -5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find time to instantaneous rest using $v = u + at$ with $v = 0, u = 12, a = -5$:
$$0 = 12 - 5t \implies t = \frac{12}{5} = 2.4\text{ s}$$

Find distance traveled using $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$:
$$0 = 12^2 - 2(5)d \implies 10d = 144 \implies d = 14.4\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
The particle decelerates up the plane under gravity alone:
$$a_{\text{retard}} = g\sin 30^\circ = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
It loses $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ of speed every second.

To lose all $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ takes:
$$t = \frac{12}{5} = 2.4\text{ s}$$
Distance is average speed times time:
$$d = \left(\frac{12 + 0}{2}\right)(2.4) = 6 \times 2.4 = 14.4\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies deceleration up the plane as $a = -g\sin 30^\circ = -5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies kinematics: $v = u + at \implies 0 = 12 - 5t \implies t = 2.4\text{ s}$; $v^2 = u^2 + 2as \implies 0 = 144 - 10d \implies d = 14.4\text{ m}$.

Add the $2.0\text{ s}$ slope descent:
$$t_{\text{total}} = 2.0 + 4.0 = 6.0\text{ s}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Acceleration, speed, and time during powered upward stage

hints: Resolve forces parallel to the plane taking up as positive: applied force $P$ pulls up while $mg\sin\theta$ opposes it down the plane.
Calculate the gravity component: $mg\sin\theta = 4.0(10)(0.6) = 24.0\text{ N}$.
Form the equation of motion $64.0 - 24.0 = 4.0a_1$ to determine the initial acceleration $a_1$.
Use kinematics equations $v_1^2 = u^2 + 2a_1 s_1$ and $v_1 = u + a_1 t_1$ from rest through distance $s_1 = 5.0\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply Newton's second law up the plane for stage 1:
$$P - mg\sin\theta = ma_1$$
$$64.0 - 4.0(10)(0.6) = 4.0a_1 \implies 64.0 - 24.0 = 4.0a_1 \implies a_1 = 10.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate speed after moving $5.0\text{ m}$ from rest:
$$v_1^2 = 0 + 2(10.0)(5.0) = 100 \implies v_1 = 10.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate duration of stage 1:
$$v_1 = u + a_1 t_1 \implies 10.0 = 0 + 10.0t_1 \implies t_1 = 1.0\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
The pulling force exceeds downhill gravity by:
$$F_{\text{net}} = 64.0 - 24.0 = 40.0\text{ N}$$
$$a_1 = \frac{40.0}{4.0} = 10.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Accelerating at $10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ over $5\text{ m}$ gives:
$$v_1 = \sqrt{2(10)(5)} = 10.0\text{ m s}^{-1}, \quad t_1 = \frac{10}{10} = 1.0\text{ s}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $F = ma$ up the plane: $P - mg\sin\theta = ma_1 \implies 64.0 - 4.0(10)(0.6) = 4.0a_1$.
Calculates $64.0 - 24.0 = 4.0a_1 \implies a_1 = 10.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Coasting distance and total apex position

hints: When $P$ is removed, the block is moving up at $10.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ but experiences an opposing force $mg\sin\theta$ down the plane.
Find the deceleration under gravity alone: $a_2 = -g\sin\theta = -10(0.6) = -6.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v = 0, u = 10.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $a = -6.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find further distance $s_2$.
Add the initial powered distance $s_1 = 5.0\text{ m}$ to $s_2$ to find the total distance $OM$ from the base.

walkthrough.text:
Identify deceleration in stage 2 under gravity alone:
$$a_2 = -g\sin\theta = -10(0.6) = -6.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate further distance $s_2$ to apex $M$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2a_2 s_2 \implies 0 = 10.0^2 - 2(6.0)s_2$$
$$12.0s_2 = 100 \implies s_2 = \frac{100}{12} = \frac{25}{3} \approx 8.33\text{ m}$$

Determine total distance $OM$:
$$OM = s_1 + s_2 = 5.0 + 8.33 = \frac{40}{3} \approx 13.3\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Once $P$ vanishes, the block coasts up against gravity:
$$a_2 = -6.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Distance traveled while coming to rest:
$$s_2 = \frac{10^2}{2(6)} = \frac{25}{3}\text{ m} \approx 8.33\text{ m}$$
$$OM = 5.0 + 8.33 = 13.3\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies deceleration under gravity after $P$ is removed: $a_2 = -g\sin\theta = -10(0.6) = -6.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Calculates $s_2 = \frac{100}{12} = \frac{25}{3} \approx 8.33\text{ m}$, giving total distance $OM = 5.0 + 8.33 = \frac{40}{3} \approx 13.3\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Return speed and total round-trip transit time

hints: At point $M$, the block comes to instantaneous rest and then accelerates down the smooth incline under gravity alone.
The acceleration down the slope is $a_3 = g\sin\theta = 6.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$ over the full distance $OM = \frac{40}{3}\text{ m}$.
Calculate return speed at $O$ using $v_{\text{return}}^2 = 0 + 2a_3(OM)$.
Sum all three stage durations: powered ascent $t_1$, coasting ascent $t_2$, and downhill return descent $t_{\text{down}}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate return speed from rest at $M$ sliding down through $OM = \frac{40}{3}\text{ m}$:
$$v_{\text{return}}^2 = 0 + 2(6.0)\left(\frac{40}{3}\right) = 160$$
$$v_{\text{return}} = \sqrt{160} \approx 12.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate duration of each phase:
$$t_1 = 1.0\text{ s}, \quad t_2 = \frac{v_1}{|a_2|} = \frac{10.0}{6.0} = 1.67\text{ s}, \quad t_{\text{down}} = \frac{\sqrt{160}}{6.0} \approx 2.11\text{ s}$$

Calculate total elapsed time:
$$t_{\text{total}} = 1.0 + 1.667 + 2.108 \approx 4.78\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
On the return slide, gravity accelerates the block down the smooth plane at $6.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$v_{\text{return}} = \sqrt{2(6.0)(13.33)} = \sqrt{160} \approx 12.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Add up all three journey segments:
$$t_1 = 1.0\text{ s}$$
$$t_2 = \frac{10}{6} = 1.67\text{ s}$$
$$t_3 = \frac{12.65}{6} = 2.11\text{ s}$$
$$t_{\text{total}} = 1.0 + 1.67 + 2.11 = 4.78\text{ s}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates return speed sliding down from rest at $M$ through $s = \frac{40}{3}\text{ m}$: $v^2 = 2(6.0)\left(\frac{40}{3}\right) = 160 \implies v = \sqrt{160} \approx 12.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Finds time to apex: $t_{\text{apex}} = t_1 + t_2 = 1.0 + \frac{10.0}{6.0} = 1.0 + 1.667 = 2.667\text{ s}$, and return descent time: $t_{\text{down}} = \frac{\sqrt{160}}{6.0} \approx 2.108\text{ s}$.
Evaluates total elapsed time: $t_{\text{total}} = 2.667 + 2.108 = 4.78\text{ s}$.
